item.title: Oct W2 26 - 01: Neural dynamics of emotionally expressive piano performance: a single-case study (Alice Mado Proverbio et al.)
item.description:
Neural dynamics of emotionally expressive piano performance: a single-case study - Alice Mado Proverbio et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.3389/fcogn.2026.1945714
Frontiers in Cognition (2026). Introduction Understanding how expert performers translate expressive intent into sound remains a central question in the neuroscience of music. We recorded continuous 128-channel EEG from a professional, internationally active concert pianist during a concert-like, uninterrupted performance (~27 min) of six works by Bach, Beethoven, and Chopin. Methods From the continuous recording, 99 two-second clean EEG segments were extracted and assigned to one of six previously validated performance-emotion categories based on independent listener evaluations (Joy, Peacefulness, Melancholy, Argumentative, Tension, Power). Each 2-s fragment contained 1,024 time points per channel, yielding 131,072 EEG data points. Cortical and subcortical source generators were reconstructed with standardized weighted Low-Resolution Electromagnetic Tomography (swLORETA), and activation was quantified both as frequency of occurrence and as dipole magnitude across three macro-regions (anterior, posterior, subcortical). Results A chi-square test on activation frequencies showed a significant association between cortical/subcortical region and emotional category. Repeated-measures ANOVAs revealed significant region- and emotion-dependent differences in dipole magnitude. Across virtually every emotional category, the left basal ganglia, left thalamus, and left precentral gyrus (BA4) emerged as the most consistently recruited generators, indicating a stable left-lateralized fronto-striato-thalamic axis subserving fine motor control within this performance. Superimposed on this stable motor substrate, emotion-specific modulations emerged: Joy was associated with the highest subcortical activation magnitude, while Melancholy showed the lowest subcortical magnitude together with a selective recruitment of right-hemisphere generators (right BA10, right somatosensory cortex, right insula), consistent with valence-based hemispheric asymmetry accounts. Pearson correlations further linked activation of the left basal ganglia, left thalamus, and left premotor cortex (BA6) to objective performance parameters (gestures per second, notes per phrase, acoustic intensity), suggesting that neurofunctional engagement scales with the motor complexity of the material performed. Discussion These findings provide a performer-side perspective complementary to models of music-evoked emotion largely derived from listeners, and suggest that, in this elite performer, expressive intent was instantiated in a specialized, left-dominant sensorimotor-limbic network modulated by affective valence. The study is complemented by animated audiovisual materials that dynamically trace the moment-to-moment evolution of LORETA source activity in synchrony with the unfolding musical passage.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 02: Musical Episodic Modulation of Human Functioning: Anticipation Mechanisms, Personal Sense, and Emotional Recall (Rodrigo Drumond Vieira)
item.description:
Musical Episodic Modulation of Human Functioning: Anticipation Mechanisms, Personal Sense, and Emotional Recall - Rodrigo Drumond Vieira - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1007/s12124-026-10033-0
Integrative Psychological and Behavioral Science (2026). This article develops a theoretical and exploratory account of musical episodic modulation of human functioning, with special attention to emotional recall. It responds to a recurrent limitation in the psychology of music: although music's effects on attention, emotion, memory, motivation, and performance have been widely documented, these domains are often examined separately rather than as mutually organized dimensions of lived episodes. The article proposes that music may function as a modulating agent of human functioning when its temporal, affective, and semantically open structure becomes coupled with ongoing activity through anticipation mechanisms. Drawing on activity theory, phenomenology of temporal consciousness, floating intentionality, entrainment, and appraisal theory, the paper conceptualizes anticipation mechanisms as the dynamic relations among anticipators, the anticipated, and horizonality. These mechanisms explain how musical signals may organize salience, attention, affect, readiness, and possible next actions over time. The argument is illustrated through a phenomenologically oriented self-study in which the same song contributed to opposed emotional episodes during two recall activities: hopelessness, yearning, and sadness in relation to the memory of a deceased father, and excitement, hope, and joy in relation to an anticipated romantic encounter. The contrast suggests that musical valence does not determine emotional outcome by itself. Rather, emotions emerge through projection-appraisal loops involving objects of thought, personal sense, belief systems, previous experience, and the unfolding music. The article concludes by outlining limitations, future research directions, and distinguishing the more specific phenomenon analyzed from the broader account of musical modulation of human functioning.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 03: Effectiveness of Behavioural Health Education Interventions in Improving Mental Health Help-Seeking Among Adult Men: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (Aneke Emeka John et al.)
item.description:
Effectiveness of Behavioural Health Education Interventions in Improving Mental Health Help-Seeking Among Adult Men: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis - Aneke Emeka John et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.63946/jebm/19495
International Journal of Evidence-Based Medicine (2026). Background: Adult men experience a disproportionate burden of mental health morbidity yet consistently demonstrate lower rates of help-seeking compared with women. Barriers such as stigma, limited mental health literacy, and masculine norms often prevent early recognition of distress and engagement with support, contributing to prolonged difficulties and poorer outcomes. Behavioural health education interventions have been proposed as a means to address these upstream barriers. Objective: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of behavioural health education interventions in improving mental health help-seeking among adult men. Methods: Following PRISMA 2020, we searched PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Dimensions AI for studies published from 2015 to 2025 for intervention studies with adult men aged ≥18 years. Ten studies were included and synthesised narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted on three RCTs reporting help-seeking intentions using the Generic Inverse Variance method, with effects expressed as Standardised Mean Differences (SMD) and 95% CIs. Findings: Narratively, interventions most consistently improved mental health awareness, stigma reduction, emotional openness, and help-seeking intentions. Evidence of direct behavioural change was limited. The pooled meta-analysis showed no statistically significant effect on help-seeking intentions (SMD = 0.02, 95% CI −0.19 to 0.24; p = 0.85; I² = 79%). Sensitivity analysis using a fixed-effect model yielded a small significant effect (SMD = 0.08, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.17). Conclusion: Behavioural health education interventions may improve psychological factors associated with help-seeking among adult men, particularly awareness, stigma-related outcomes, and readiness to seek support. However, the meta-analysis found no statistically significant pooled effect on help-seeking intentions, with substantial heterogeneity indicating variation according to intervention type, population characteristics, and delivery context.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 04: Sensory Processing and Executive Functioning Interaction in Neurodevelopmental Disorders and At-Risk Conditions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (Stefano Scatigna et al.)
item.description:
Sensory Processing and Executive Functioning Interaction in Neurodevelopmental Disorders and At-Risk Conditions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis - Stefano Scatigna et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2026.107010
Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews (2026). This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the relationship between sensory processing (SP) and executive functioning (EF) in children and adolescents (ages 0-18) diagnosed with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) or at-risk conditions, such as prematurity and genetic syndromes. Adhering to PRISMA guidelines, the results of 30 peer-reviewed studies were analyzed by qualitative and quantitative analyses to evaluate the strength and nature of these associations. The findings revealed a consistent and significant correlation between SP and EF, with effect sizes (r) ranging from r =.19 to r =.77. Meta-analytic synthesis confirmed a medium effect size (d =.58). While substantial heterogeneity was observed (I^2 = 82.9%), it was not moderated by the specific diagnosis of NDDs, age, EF component or correlation adjustment status. Notably, assessment modality served as a significant moderator: performance-based measures demonstrated higher associative strength and lower heterogeneity compared to questionnaire-based or combined assessment. Regression models indicated that SP measures statistically accounted for a substantial portion of EF variance (28-71%), while comparative analyses showed moderate-to-large differences in EF performance (η² =.10-.34) between typical and atypical sensory profiles. Furthermore, mediation analyses suggested significant indirect associations involving EF, particularly emotion regulation and inhibitory control, in the relationship between sensory processing and adaptive and functional outcomes. The evidence underscores a robust interdependence between sensory processing and executive functions in clinical and at-risk pediatric populations. These findings highlight the potential relevance of considering both sensory and executive domains in assessment and intervention planning.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 05: The impact of social isolation on the development of alcohol use and alcohol addiction-related processes in animals: a systematic review (Sofie van Koppen et al.)
item.description:
The impact of social isolation on the development of alcohol use and alcohol addiction-related processes in animals: a systematic review - Sofie van Koppen et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2026.107016
Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews (2026). Social isolation significantly shapes drinking behaviour, acting as both a risk and protective factor. Animal models provide controlled causal examination of how social isolation shapes alcohol-related behaviours and underlying mechanisms. This systematic review examined how social isolation shapes the subsequent development of alcohol consumption and addiction-related processes in mammals from an alcohol-naïve baseline, evaluating the moderating roles of sex and age of isolation onset. Systematic searches of Embase, PubMed, and PsycInfo up to April 2026 identified 66 studies comparing alcohol consumption or addiction-related processes between isolated and socially housed mammals. Social isolation was associated with higher alcohol consumption and enhanced motivation across behavioural paradigms, though these effects were highly dependent on age of isolation onset and other moderating factors. Isolation at weaning age produced stronger effects than isolation in adulthood. Evidence for sex as a moderator remained inconsistent. Across fourteen studies of neurobiological outcomes, the clearest pattern was elevated dopaminergic and noradrenergic signalling in isolated animals following alcohol exposure, particularly at higher doses, while GABAergic, opioidergic, and serotonergic systems showed more region- and subunit-specific effects. In conclusion, social isolation shapes alcohol consumption in a manner that is highly dependent on moderating factors, alongside corresponding alterations in reward processing and stress reactivity that may underlie these behavioural patterns. Age of isolation onset emerged as a consistent moderator. These findings provide a preliminary mechanistic explanation of how social isolation shapes the development of alcohol use and alcohol use disorder, while also highlighting how methodological decisions in preclinical addiction research shape outcomes.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 06: SEXUAL HEALTH IN RHEUMATIC AND MUSCULOSKELETAL DISEASES: A CRITICAL NARRATIVE REVIEW FROM MEASUREMENT TO CARE (Pedro Henrique de Barcelos Lavareda et al.)
item.description:
SEXUAL HEALTH IN RHEUMATIC AND MUSCULOSKELETAL DISEASES: A CRITICAL NARRATIVE REVIEW FROM MEASUREMENT TO CARE - Pedro Henrique de Barcelos Lavareda et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.70773/revistatopicos/790713064
Revista Tópicos. (2026). Este trabalho visa analisar criticamente como a saúde sexual e seu impacto psicossocial têm sido conceituados, mensurados e incorporados ao cuidado de pessoas com doenças reumáticas e musculoesqueléticas. Para isso, foi conduzida uma revisão crítica de escopo pan-reumático, orientada por uma busca estruturada por diretrizes, consensos, revisões sistemáticas, metanálises e estudos qualitativos relevantes. A literatura converge quanto à elevada frequência de dificuldades sexuais, associadas à dor, fadiga, rigidez, limitação funcional, secura genital, vasculopatia, alterações da imagem corporal, sofrimento psíquico, efeitos farmacológicos e tensões relacionais. Entretanto, as prevalências agregadas apresentam heterogeneidade, predomínio de estudos transversais, baixa avaliação do sofrimento clinicamente relevante e instrumentos centrados no desempenho genital, no binarismo de gênero e na atividade sexual recente. Diretrizes reumatológicas contemporâneas tratam em detalhes de contracepção, fertilidade, gestação, lactação e segurança medicamentosa, mas não equivalem a diretrizes de saúde sexual integral. Prazer, autonomia, identidade, comunicação, violência, discriminação e justiça sexual permanecem periféricos. De modo geral, constatou-se que a sexualidade é um desfecho legítimo de saúde e de participação social, não um apêndice reprodutivo nem um simples marcador de função erétil ou vaginal. Nesse aspecto, estudos voltados à medidas multidimensionais cocriadas, coortes longitudinais, ensaios pragmáticos, pesquisa de implementação e amostras interseccionais são necessários.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 07: Managing Emotions at Work: A TCCM Systematic Literature Review of Empirical Emotional Labour Research (Shuyu Zhang et al.)
item.description:
Managing Emotions at Work: A TCCM Systematic Literature Review of Empirical Emotional Labour Research - Shuyu Zhang et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1002/pchj.70118
PsyCh Journal (2026). Emotional labour (EL) has become a serious concern in the modern workplace due to the rapid development of the service-oriented economy. Existing literature reviews of emotional labour studies leave many questions unexplored. This study addresses these questions by conducting a holistic review of 143 high-impact empirical articles published in peer-reviewed journals from APA PsycInfo, EBSCO Academic Search Premier, Scopus, and Web of Science using the TCCM framework (Theory-Context-Characteristics-Methodology). The document search process is visualised with a PRISMA diagram. We point out several future directions for scholars who are interested in emotional labour. For example, emotional labour research needs to transition from cross-sectional designs to multi-wave designs. Most importantly, this study serves as a roadmap for scholars to navigate the complexity of emotional labour research and provides practitioners with evidence-based strategies to mitigate the negative influence of emotional labour.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 01: Body percussion and the biomechanical calibration of musical meter: the somatic externalization of meter hypothesis (Francisco Javier Romero Naranjo)
item.description:
Body percussion and the biomechanical calibration of musical meter: the somatic externalization of meter hypothesis - Francisco Javier Romero Naranjo - 2026 https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1905062
Frontiers in Psychology (2026). Musical meter takes specific forms, a preferred tempo and a small set of stable subdivisions, that existing accounts do not fully explain. I propose the Somatic Externalization of Meter (SEM) hypothesis: that these parameters are calibrated to the oscillatory dynamics of the moving body, so meter inherits the characteristic periods of the limbs. The proposal comprises a well-supported causal claim that bodily and vestibular state shape how an ambiguous rhythm is heard, a central mechanistic claim that beat perception is parameterized by effector biomechanics, and a conjectural claim about manufactured percussion. Body percussion is the diagnostic case, in which effector and instrument coincide, giving a zero-offset baseline against which instrumental displacement is measured. I recast the mechanistic claim as a measurable quantity, biomechanical transparency , which admits a strict null, and set out eight falsifiable predictions. Two existing findings run against the hypothesis and are reported.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 02: Modeling the rhythmic complexity of professional drumming with an oscillation-driven reservoir computer (Yuji Kawai et al.)
item.description:
Modeling the rhythmic complexity of professional drumming with an oscillation-driven reservoir computer - Yuji Kawai et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1007/s11571-026-10512-5
Cognitive Neurodynamics (2026). Musical performances, particularly in drumming, are characterized not only by their structured rhythmic patterns but also by the subtle variations in timing and amplitude series that create expressive complexity. This study proposes a neural-inspired computational model to investigate how the brain might learn and internalize such complex rhythms. Inspired by the established roles of the cerebellum and basal ganglia in production of rhythms and timings, we utilize an oscillation-driven reservoir computer, a recurrent neural network model for temporal learning, to simulate the generation of human-like expressive drumming performances. First, the model was trained to replicate Jeff Porcaro's distinctive hi-hat patterns. Analyses revealed that the outputs of the model incorporating high-frequency oscillators ([50, 100] Hz), closely matched the original drumming, reproducing its characteristic fluctuations and patterns in inter-beat timings (microtiming) and amplitudes. Next, the model was trained to generate multidimensional drum kit performances for various genres (funk, jazz, samba, and rock). The model's outputs exhibited timing deviation and audio features characteristic of the original performances. Our findings demonstrate that oscillation-driven reservoir computing can replicate the rhythmic complexity of professional drumming, suggesting it as a potential computational principle for motor timing and rhythm generation. This approach provides a powerful framework for understanding how the brain generates and processes intricate rhythmic patterns. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s11571-026-10512-5.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 03: Impacts of digital third-wave interventions for adults on wellbeing and mental health outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (Tom Curtis Gordon et al.)
item.description:
Impacts of digital third-wave interventions for adults on wellbeing and mental health outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials - Tom Curtis Gordon et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pdig.0001764
PLOS Digital Health (2026). To synthesise the efficacy of digital third-wave process-based interventions (e.g., ACT, Mindfulness, Compassion) for improving wellbeing and ameliorating mental health symptoms in adults. A prospectively registered systematic review (OSF: 10.17605/OSF.IO/5RMU2) and random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) was conducted across six databases through January 2026. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework. Interventions (k = 147; N = 26,391) yielded small-to-moderate immediate post-intervention improvements in wellbeing (k = 46, g = 0.36), depression (k = 110, g = 0.44), anxiety (k = 93, g = 0.40), stress (k = 66, g = 0.46), quality of life (k = 32, g = 0.30), and psychological flexibility (k = 51, g = 0.41). Heterogeneity was substantial across most outcomes (I2 > 75%). Benefits were observed across healthy (61 trials; n = 15,770), mental health (41 trials; n = 6,130), and medical samples (46 trials; n = 4,491), with population type not significantly moderating immediate post-intervention effects. Comparator type significantly moderated several analyses, with smaller effects against active than inactive controls. Guidance did not significantly moderate immediate post-intervention effects, although it predicted larger short-term depression effects (QM = 4.17, p = .048). At short-term follow-up, effects remained statistically supported across all outcomes, while only depression, anxiety, and stress remained statistically supported at medium-term follow-up. GRADE certainty was moderate for most immediate post-intervention outcomes and low for quality of life. Digital third-wave interventions produced small-to-moderate average benefits across symptom-focused, wellbeing-focused, and process outcomes. Effects were smaller against active comparators, indicating that pooled benefits should be interpreted in relation to comparator intensity. Future research should prioritise rigorous active controls, longer follow-up, and direct tests of whether changes in psychological flexibility mediate improvements in symptoms and wellbeing.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 04: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis (Jingwen Li et al.)
item.description:
How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis - Jingwen Li et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dcn.2026.101831
Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience (2026). The effects of school-based interventions (SBIs) on children’s neurodevelopment are poorly synthesized. This systematic review integrates neuroscientific evidence on how structured educational activities influence brain development in children aged 3-12 years. Following PRISMA guidelines, we identified 17 empirical studies (published 2014–2025) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). Of these, 8 studies were included in a random-effects meta-analysis and all 17 in a thematic synthesis. The meta-analysis revealed a preliminary association between SBIs and reduced amygdala activity during stress regulation tasks ( r = –.28, 95% CI [–.50, –.02]), based on two studies, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. No significant pooled effect for executive function, likely due to high heterogeneity. Thematic analysis distinguishes between mechanisms of plasticity and markers of intervention effectiveness: the first three characterize intra-individual mechanisms of experience-dependent plasticity, including (1) executive function interventions engaged prefrontal networks through both increased recruitment and enhanced neural efficiency; (2) socio-emotional programs modulated limbic-prefrontal circuits; (3) language and auditory programs shaped sensory-specific electrophysiological markers and cortical specialization; and the fourth theme identifies a neural marker of the effective process of intervention delivery, demonstrating that (4) teacher-child inter-brain synchrony was positively correlated with learning outcomes. By integrating findings across neural, cognitive, and affective domains, this review provides a conceptual framework linking pedagogical practices to neural plasticity and advances the understanding of the neurofunctional pathways through which educational experiences shape the developing brain.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 05: CHUNK-BASED COMMUNICATIVE LANGUAGE TEACHING AND ITS IMPACT ON INDONESIAN EFL STUDENTS’ SPEAKING FLUENCY: A NARRATIVE REVIEW (Muhammad Pandu Khoiron et al.)
item.description:
CHUNK-BASED COMMUNICATIVE LANGUAGE TEACHING AND ITS IMPACT ON INDONESIAN EFL STUDENTS’ SPEAKING FLUENCY: A NARRATIVE REVIEW - Muhammad Pandu Khoiron et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.31943/wej.v10i2.744
Wiralodra English Journal (2026). The current narrative literature review aimed to investigate the use of Chunk-Based CLT as a pedagogical technique to enhance the fluency of EFL students from Indonesia. Even though the students have been receiving formal English education in all stages from primary to tertiary levels, many still experience difficulties in their fluency due to the high cognitive load and their tendency to translate from word to word. In order to explore this problem, the literature synthesis was performed using academic works related to formulaic language and communicative pedagogy. It turned out that lexical chunks (prefabricated formulaic sequences) help learners acquire important cognitive shortcuts and minimize unnatural pausing, increase speech rate and reduce the anxiety about making grammatical mistakes during language learning in a foreign language. Besides, engaging the learners with these linguistic units in communicative activities is beneficial for producing natural speech. Thus, the pedagogical relevance of this method of instruction in EFL context is highly significant. Based on the findings made, this paper shows that the chunk-based instruction is useful in bridging the fluency gap. To continue this research, further empirical studies need to be performed experimentally.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 06: Sexual Dysregulation After Traumatic Brain Injury and Stroke: A Critical Narrative Review of Neurobiology, Clinical Phenotypes, and Management (Rocco Salvatore Calabrò et al.)
item.description:
Sexual Dysregulation After Traumatic Brain Injury and Stroke: A Critical Narrative Review of Neurobiology, Clinical Phenotypes, and Management - Rocco Salvatore Calabrò et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.3390/brainsci16090995
Brain Sciences (2026). Background/Objectives: Acquired brain injury (ABI) can disturb sexual regulation, but the literature does not support a single lesion-to-behavior relationship. This critical narrative review evaluates hypersexuality, sexual disinhibition, and rare acquired paraphilic manifestations after traumatic brain injury (TBI) and stroke, and asks how sparse, heterogeneous evidence can inform proportionate clinical care. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to 6 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and full texts. Evidence appraisal considered methodological quality, directness, and competing explanations. Thirteen English-language case-based publications were assessed, with neurological observations distinguished from pharmacological comparators. Results: Sexual dysfunction is common after ABI, whereas dysregulated sexual behavior is less frequent and poorly quantified. TBI primarily supports a distributed vulnerability model involving diffuse axonal injury and disruption of frontal regulatory connections. Stroke can nominate strategic candidate nodes, but lesion-network effects and clinical context remain decisive. Clinical observations associate inappropriate sexual behavior with broader behavioral difficulties, without establishing a uniform syndrome. Recent guidelines support individualized sexuality care, while contemporary imaging studies strengthen network plausibility without directly establishing sexual-dysregulation mechanisms. Conclusions: A phenotype-first framework separates dysfunction from dysregulation and distinguishes direct clinical evidence from mechanistic extrapolation. Assessment should establish what changed and whether reversible contributors explain the behavior before assigning a persistent phenotype. Management should match the dominant clinical problem, preserve consensual intimacy, and use the least restrictive targeted strategy. Explicit monitoring should determine whether benefit justifies continued treatment. Case-based evidence and language-restricted selection limit generalizability; prospective studies require standardized phenotypes and repeated observation across settings.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 07: Clarifying Online Cooperative Learning in EFL Contexts: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, the Five Core Elements, and Implementation Challenges (Zhang Aijia et al.)
item.description:
Clarifying Online Cooperative Learning in EFL Contexts: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, the Five Core Elements, and Implementation Challenges - Zhang Aijia et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.26803/ijlter.25.8.18
International Journal of Learning Teaching and Educational Research (2026). Although online cooperative learning has been widely examined in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, it is often conceptually blurred with less structured forms of collaborative learning. This review synthesised empirical articles on online cooperative learning in EFL contexts, focusing on study characteristics, reported outcomes, the operationalisation of Johnson and Johnson’s five elements, and implementation challenges. PRISMA 2020, Eric, Web of Science, Scopus, and ProQuest were searched for empirical English-language journal articles published up to June 2026. Twenty-five studies met the eligibility criteria and were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Mixed-methods designs were the most common (56%, n = 14), university settings dominated the studies (80%, n = 20), and writing was the leading focus (40%, n = 10). Of the 17 studies using inferential tests of language-related performance, 16 reported statistically significant positive gains or associations, although the strength of evidence varied. Positive interdependence was explicitly reported in 20 studies and implied in 5. In contrast, small-group skills and group processing were explicitly reported in only[1] 3 and 7 studies, respectively. The main implementation challenges involved weak technological–pedagogical alignment, insufficient instructional scaffolding, and uneven participation and accountability. The findings suggest that online cooperative learning should be conceptualized not according to named cooperative structures alone, but according to how the online cooperative EFL learning environment, instructional configuration, and the five core cooperative learning elements are integrated. Future research should design clearly structured online cooperative EFL courses across more diverse educational settings, language areas, and learner groups, particularly for learners with lower language proficiency or limited digital literacy.
